tasks.title: Make qa.py display-check report a locked desktop session
tasks.description: HANDOFF lesson of the 2026-10-01 unattended run: "`qa.py display-check` does not detect a GNOME lock." The evidence owner runs `display-check` before taking display :0 and when handing it back (.agents/skills/gitturtle-native-qa/references/visual-evidence.md), but a locked GNOME session passes it, and keys and captures sent to a locked session are wasted: the shield covers the window and Mutter input reaches the lock screen. `display.check` (scripts/native_qa/display.py:67) prints `date -u`, foreign GitTurtle and driver processes and windows, and returns an exit code; its tests are in scripts/native_qa/test_display.py (for example `test_unreadable_display_is_inconclusive` and `test_missing_pgrep_is_inconclusive`). Checked on this host on 2026-10-02: GNOME Shell 50.1 exposes `org.gnome.ScreenSaver` at `/org/gnome/ScreenSaver` on the session bus with `GetActive(out b active)` (it returned `(false,)` unlocked), `ActiveChanged` and `Lock`, and systemd 259's logind reports `LockedHint=no` for the graphical (Wayland) session. Decision (coordinator, 2026-10-02, delegated by the owner): display-check reads both sources through fixed argument arrays with a short timeout (`gdbus call --session` to `GetActive`, and `loginctl show-session` with `-p LockedHint` for the graphical session); either one reporting a lock fails the check with a line naming its source; when neither can be read it prints an inconclusive line and exits as an unreadable display does; it never locks, unlocks, wakes or changes the session. Reason: either source alone misses a case (a GNOME shield with logind lagging, or a desktop with logind only), both are read-only, and an inconclusive result keeps today's meaning for an unreadable display. The task needs no external evidence: the unit tests and the tooling gate prove it. It edits the package plan item 5 extends (`qa.py scenario`, `recheck`), so it runs after item 5 lands. Suggested as the pilot's task without external evidence (plan item 9), because every app Rust change in this queue carries the native profile.

acceptance.description: `qa.py display-check` exits 1 with a line naming the source when GNOME ScreenSaver's `GetActive` returns true or logind's `LockedHint` is yes for the graphical session, and its output and exit code are otherwise unchanged when both report unlocked; unit tests in scripts/native_qa/test_display.py cover a lock reported by each source, both unlocked, and the argument arrays of the stubbed commands.

When neither source can be read (no session bus, `gdbus` or `loginctl` missing, a timeout or unparseable output), display-check prints an inconclusive lock line and exits with the code an unreadable display uses; unit tests cover each case without a real bus.

Every command display-check builds only reads state: none calls `Lock`, `SetActive`, `SimulateUserActivity` or a `loginctl` lock, unlock or activate verb, asserted by a test over the argument arrays it builds.
scripts/native_qa/README.md's display-check row names the two lock sources, the failing and inconclusive results and which desktops each source covers.

tasks.title: Reveal a keyboard-focused row in the frame that first draws its focus
tasks.description: Follow-up (7) of the `tab-reveals-branch-and-tag-rows` design review (#136, HANDOFF). `focus_reveal::FocusReveal` (crates/app/src/focus_reveal.rs, from #136) measures the focused control's bounds while the container's children prepaint and applies the reveal after painting through `window.defer` (:195; module docs :9-11), so #136's native probe saw the newly focused row unrevealed, its ring cut at the list's edge, for one 6 to 12 ms frame on 2 of 8 scrolling keys (its docs/validation.md entry, ~:89). Users: the branch chooser (branch_actions.rs:948) and the remote manager (:1223), the tag inspector (tags.rs:143) and Tags (:296) with `Trigger::Keyboard`, and the project hub body (projects.rs:119, `Trigger::AnyFocus`, 12 px margin, `reveal_on_focus` :579-584). Settings' Your themes rows already reveal within the frame: `reveal_in_page` (settings.rs:121-135) sets the page offset during render from the last frame's bounds, and `reveal_focused_row` (theme_editor.rs:325-340) uses `scroll_to_item`, which the uniform_list applies in its own prepaint (settings.rs:75). Decision (coordinator, 2026-10-02, delegated by the owner): every FocusReveal user applies the reveal before the frame that first draws the new focus is painted, with the rule unchanged (least scroll to the nearest edge plus the ring room, no animation; a click and a redraw without a focus change scroll nothing; the hub keeps its 12 px and its click reveal). The mechanism is the implementer's (for example computing the offset when focus changes from the bounds the last frame recorded, as `reveal_in_page` does, or laying the container out again within the frame); a later frame may refine the offset but no painted frame may show the control cut. Reason: a ring cut for one frame is a visible flicker on every scrolling key, and Settings shows the toolkit allows a same-frame reveal. DESIGN.md:333 then says the list scrolls in the frame that first draws the focus, as its theme-editor sentence (:162) does. No list in this task marks a selected row (the chooser, remote manager and Tags rows set no `.selected`), so focused rows are the only row state. Hard: GPUI's frame order (layout, prepaint, paint, deferred effects) decides what can be measured when, and the test must observe individual painted frames.

acceptance.description: A GPUI view test records, for every frame painted after each real `tab` and `shift-tab` keystroke through the branch chooser with 30 branches at 1000 × 680, the focused row's painted bounds grown by the installed ring's gap plus width and the list's visible bounds (for example from the bounds FocusReveal already observes in prepaint), and asserts that no painted frame shows the row outside the list; the same for Tags with 30 tags. It fails on origin/main, whose first frame after a scrolling key paints the row cut.

The project hub reveals a focused field 12 px clear of the page's edges in the first frame painted after a keyboard or a pointer focus change, asserted by the same per-frame recording, and `keyboard_focus_reveals_project_fields_and_submit_at_small_window` (projects.rs:1513) passes.
